clue.text: Affected by contents of gallery, supposing functionary's kicked off

parts.note: what hangs in a gallery is art
supposing means if

indicators.note: kicked tells us the word off is booted out of the functionary, leaving the rest

parts.note: a functionary is an official; the 's is a link
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone's manner seems put on, influenced by the gallery's paintings and an official being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked off' reads as a phrasal verb meaning dismissed, but it splits into the deletion signal and the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected behaviour is put on and unnatural, which is a synonym sense of artificial.

clue.text: Fierce beast, one disabled without its tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the word for a disabled person is dropped

parts.note: a crock is an old or disabled person, informally

explanation.surface: A ferocious animal, already crippled, has also lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc, short for crocodile, is a fierce reptile and so a fierce beast.

clue.text: A position the indolent took for eating

explanation.surface: A pose the lazy adopted at mealtimes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the Lotus-eaters ate a fruit that made them idle and forgetful; the lotus position is a cross-legged yoga pose.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is both a cross-legged yoga posture and the fruit eaten by Homer's idle Lotus-eaters.

clue.text: So unruly, one misbehaves with disastrous consequences

indicators.note: misbehaves tells us the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone so badly behaved acts up, with calamitous results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaves' signals rearranging SOUNRULY plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinously is an adverb meaning in a way that brings ruin, so with disastrous consequences.

clue.text: Survey of artistic period covering up deception

indicators.note: covering up means the period's name is wrapped round the deception

parts.note: the Renaissance was the great European period of art
a con is a deception or trick

explanation.surface: A study of an era of art that hides some fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deception' tempts as the definition, but the definition is 'Survey', a military scouting mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance is an exploratory survey, especially a military inspection of territory.

clue.text: Plug connecting to a different port?

definitions.text: Plug connecting to a different port?

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: different says the letters of port appear in another order

explanation.surface: A connector that lets a plug fit a socket of another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges PORT into PTOR; 'connecting to' joins the pieces. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is a device that lets a plug fit an incompatible socket or port.

clue.text: Went as a body to move abroad, receiving nothing in return

indicators.note: in return tells us the whole assembled word is read backwards
receiving means another letter is taken inside the verb

parts.note: to deport someone is to move them abroad by force
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: People went in a group to emigrate, getting nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts O into DEPORT to make DEPOORT; 'in return' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: To troop is to walk together in a group, so trooped means moved as a body.

clue.text: Tree: preserving one is deliberate

indicators.note: preserving means holding something safe inside, so the verb keeps one within it

parts.note: to deliberate is to confer, to discuss
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tree is deliberately kept alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliberate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, confer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir.

clue.text: Composer's endlessly clean, spartan accommodation

definitions.note: Composer's here is Composer is, the 's a link

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for clean loses its final letter

parts.note: clean means pure
a cell is a bare, austere room, as for a monk or prisoner

explanation.surface: A musician's lodgings are relentlessly tidy and bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PURE to PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was an English Baroque composer of the 17th century.

clue.text: Force long underground, initially to be confused with reserve?

definitions.text: initially to be confused with reserve?

explanation.surface: An army buried for ages, whose initials might be mistaken for a reserve force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Terracotta Army is China's buried clay army; its initials TA match the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, now renamed the Army Reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The terracotta figures are an army force buried in Xi'an for over two thousand years.

clue.text: Killer in film avoiding northern city

indicators.note: in places the killer inside what remains of the film
avoiding means the film genre does without the letter for northern

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film
an orc is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A murderer in a movie steers clear of a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern city' tempts as one phrase, but 'northern' supplies the letter removed; 'Killer' is the whale, not a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is a cathedral city in the English West Midlands.

clue.text: Deer has one tongue

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A deer possesses a single tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a language of India, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Speaker's to wallow in this part

indicators.note: Speaker's says the word for wallow is heard, not seen, when spoken

parts.note: to wallow is to roll about, as in mud

explanation.surface: An orator is set to luxuriate in this theatrical part.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is an actor's part in a play or film.

clue.text: No pseudonym that should be spelled with a capital

definitions.text: that should be spelled with a capital

explanation.surface: A real name, which needs an initial capital letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A proper name is someone's real name rather than a pen name, and in grammar a proper noun, written with a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name is both a genuine name, not an alias, and a noun that takes a capital letter.

clue.text: Ancient Scottish cauldron's contents

indicators.note: contents says the answer lies inside the word cauldron's

explanation.surface: What's inside a Scottish cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' signals the letters inside 'cauldron's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Auld is the Scots word for old, so ancient in Scottish usage.

clue.text: Bit he chucked into pool that held tax receipts

indicators.note: into places the jumbled letters inside the pool

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake or pool

indicators.note: chucked means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man threw something into a pond that once stored taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarn is a northern English word for a small mountain lake; tithes were a tenth of farm produce owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn stored the tenth of produce paid as tax to the church.

clue.text: Rescue from drowning one in unfamiliar element

explanation.surface: Saving someone from drowning, and a person out of their depth.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb phrase it is to pull something from the water; as a noun it is a person ill at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish out of water is to retrieve something from it; a fish out of water is someone uncomfortable in strange surroundings.

clue.text: He sits on cases, needing my power ultimately to close one

indicators.note: to close means the letter comes at the very end, shutting off one

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of power

explanation.surface: A judge needs final authority to shut down a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive. 'ultimately' gives R, and 'to close' places it after ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner presides over inquests into deaths, sitting in judgement on cases.

clue.text: Believer in spirits taken up in a cloud of steam

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means read upwards, so the words in a are reversed

parts.note: a mist is a cloud of fine droplets, like steam

explanation.surface: A spiritualist is carried up in a haze of vapour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses INA into ANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An animist believes that spirits live in natural objects and places.

clue.text: After temperature's dropped, insert synthetic polymer

indicators.note: synthetic means artificially put together, so the letters are reassembled
dropped says the temperature letter is let fall from the word insert

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Once the heat is gone, put in a man-made plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes T from INSERT to leave INSER, which 'synthetic' rearranges. 'synthetic polymer' looks like one phrase, but 'synthetic' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance, natural or man-made, which is often a polymer.

clue.text: Horse's messy saddle put into cold washing solution

definitions.note: Horse's here is Horse is, the 's a link

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: put into places the jumbled letters inside the washing liquid

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution used for washing

indicators.note: messy says the letters of saddle are in disorder

explanation.surface: A horse's untidy saddle is plunged into cold soapy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse's' is Horse is, with the 's as link; lye is an old alkaline washing liquid made from wood ash.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught horse.

clue.text: It's a question about pop

parts.note: read literally, an enquiry after the health of one's dad; the phrase is also British slang for sexual activity

explanation.surface: A query concerning dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop is dad, so the clue is a friendly enquiry about your father; in British slang the phrase is also a humorous term for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally asks after a father's wellbeing, father being pop.

clue.text: One giving time to warn at intervals about leading element of enemy?

definitions.text: One giving time to warn at intervals about leading element of enemy?

parts.note: a watch is a device that tells the time

indicators.note: about means the alternate letters go round the enemy's first letter
at intervals takes every other letter of the word warn
leading element picks the first letter of enemy

explanation.surface: A lookout's job is to sound alarms now and then about an enemy's approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes W and R from WARN; 'about' puts E, from 'leading element of enemy', between them. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchtower is a lookout post from which sentries give warning of approaching enemies.

clue.text: Sounding more complaining after new infection

indicators.note: sounding says the phrase is to be heard as spoken

parts.note: moanier means more complaining; put it after new and you say new moanier

explanation.surface: Sounding even grumpier after catching a fresh infection.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are read in reverse of their clue order because of 'after'; spoken together they give the lung disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is a lung infection.

clue.text: Cock robin's head, eyes, and most of back

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of robin's

parts.note: two eyes look like the letters O and O

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the word for back

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A male bird inspected through a robin's head, eyes and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cock, the adult male chicken.

clue.text: Roof support is stone, for power

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A ceiling prop is made of stone to give it strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link here but PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a timber post supporting the roof of a mine tunnel.

clue.text: Country that is kept in its place by Russian banks

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Russian

parts.words: that is kept in its place
parts.note: a river is the thing kept in its place by banks, and with Russian banks it is the Ural

explanation.surface: A nation held in position by Russia's financial institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' means riverbanks, not lenders: the Ural is a river between Russian banks. 'Country' is an adjective here, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective means of the countryside, which is what rural means.

clue.text: Policy to cover on the inside

explanation.surface: A policy to protect from within.
explanation.walkthrough: A party line is its policy; to line a coat is to cover its inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is an official policy, as in the party line, and to line something is to cover its inner surface.
